scope: Complete original and two complete revised mathematical/editorial reads of the fibration and local-ideal inputs; the second follows the first production build and images. The unchanged fibration original is the complete checkpoint272 second read reused before editing; the original local-ideal input is freshly read. Final guard-only repairs receive direct affected-source and rebuilt-image checks. This is not a fresh whole-Chapter1 or whole-Chapter15 review.

subjects.subject: Plurisubharmonic functions
subjects.developed: Chapter 1 contains the general psh calculus, local correction, compactness, products, capacity, regularization, local ideals, divisorial estimates and descent. Its polar-measure calculus includes inverse maximum and variation-capacity estimates; Holder potentials give trace-mass and path-distance bounds. The ideal calculus now includes cancellation of a common quasi-plurisubharmonic summand, proved by subtracting its finite Lelong number on every local modification.
subjects.boundary: Classical global analytic regularization and local ideal theory retain explicit imported inputs. A nonclosed background is handled by a smooth local correction, not a local potential for that background. Holder distance control is not a bounded-potential theorem.
subjects.disposition_scope: Developed counterpart or retained tool at the stated scope; remaining generalizations are delimited below. Subject coverage is not a theorem-by-theorem transfer.

subjects.subject: Non-pluripolar products
subjects.developed: Chapter 1 provides bounded calculus; Chapters 6-8 construct extended products, finite damping and tail criteria and exhibit infinite mass.
subjects.boundary: Extended top mass can be infinite despite integrable current coefficients. Capacity convergence alone gives neither undamped mass control nor total-variation convergence.

subjects.boundary: An envelope-class condition is not a uniform mass bound. A solution in a relative envelope class need not differ boundedly from its reference.

subjects.subject: Comparison of singularities
subjects.developed: Chapter 15 gives the ideal L1 metric and its curve completion, and a nonseparated uniformity on all ordinary classes using both envelopes, controlled ideals and fixed-model divisorial variation. Chapter 18 identifies the source topology on atomic curve data. Chapter 29 constructs complete model metrics under positive lower volume and bounded mass, and the complete polar-variation geometry of all curve models including zero mass. On curves the ordinary uniformity is envelope L1 plus atomic variation; its canonical ideal locus is complete but the whole ordinary space is incomplete. Chapter 31 treats varying-reference equations. Sections 15.6.4 and 29.12.3 develop convergence for every smooth obstacle. The resulting uniformity is covariant under smooth gauges and positive scaling, and its analytic closure is exactly ordinary/ideal envelope equality for all smooth obstacles. On curves this closure equals the zero-obstacle closure. The new pseudometric has complete canonical ideal loci, while the whole ordinary space remains incomplete even on a fixed positive-mass model family. On ordinary curve models its topology is strictly between the zero-obstacle topology and polar total variation.
subjects.boundary: The original upper-volume comparison can fail the triangle inequality. Its complete replacement prevents approach to zero lower volume. The ordinary uniformity is strictly weaker than polar variation on general curve models. Paired background/obstacle transport is exact. With zero obstacles fixed, every nonconstant smooth gauge between positive curve backgrounds of equal area is discontinuous in both directions, already in a positive-mass cutoff. The complete polar-variation metric remains gauge invariant after ordinary projection. Extending the stronger complete model topology beyond its current mass regimes remains open. All-obstacle convergence restores smooth-gauge covariance but remains nonseparated on ordinary classes and incomplete on general curve models. Its analytic closure requires equality at every smooth obstacle. This is equivalent to zero-obstacle equality on curves and, in higher dimension, under bounded mass with positive lower volume of the ideal representative. Relative-envelope membership suffices in any smooth background; the remaining zero-lower-volume and no-BMP implications are unresolved here. Polar total variation remains the stronger complete curve-model topology.

subjects.subject: I-good singularities
subjects.developed: Chapter 15 proves analytic envelope equality, ordered ideal-envelope convergence and, for every positive Hermitian background, closure and sequential closure of analytic ordinary classes exactly at equality of the two envelopes. Rational curvature corrections remain in the fixed background and satisfy all controlled ideal weights. Chapter 29 retains the separate volume characterization and complete analytic-model approximation under bounded mass and positive lower volume. Sections 15.6.4 and 29.12.3 develop convergence for every smooth obstacle. The resulting uniformity is covariant under smooth gauges and positive scaling, and its analytic closure is exactly ordinary/ideal envelope equality for all smooth obstacles. On curves this closure equals the zero-obstacle closure. The new pseudometric has complete canonical ideal loci, while the whole ordinary space remains incomplete even on a fixed positive-mass model family. On ordinary curve models its topology is strictly between the zero-obstacle topology and polar total variation. Relative-envelope membership gives equality at every smooth obstacle; in the bounded-mass positive-lower-ideal-volume regime, zero-obstacle equality is sufficient. Divisorial products of curve potentials have an exact reduction of both obstacle envelopes to curve envelopes and a zero-model-volume all-obstacle criterion, with nonanalytic ordinary-type examples in every dimension at least two. Weighted prime divisors on compact holomorphic submersions reduce both obstacle envelopes exactly to the base, provided each component dominates the base and every fiber meets the complement. The divisors may be singular or ramified; all relevant ordinary representatives still have zero extended mass. A positive curve base gives the zero-obstacle/all-obstacle criterion. An explicit Hopf-threefold product gives a nonanalytic ordinary type with all-obstacle equality and zero model volumes while the ambient Hermitian background fails bounded mass. Relative-envelope membership of a divisorial fibration type is exactly membership of its base type, including relative to the corresponding ideal models. All-obstacle ordinary/ideal equality upstairs is equivalent to all-obstacle equality on the base. The explicit multiplier-ideal factorization requires relative simple normal crossings. A smooth branched graph in a projective product violates that formula at weight 3/4, while the envelope reduction holds. A smooth incidence divisor in the product of a projective plane and a projective line contains a complete fiber. Its induced zero obstacle diverges there, but a maximum-principle calculation gives an explicit bounded base correction and equal ordinary/ideal models, zero singularity volumes and equality at all smooth obstacles. This is an explicit example, not a general extension of the finite-obstacle theorem. Relative-envelope membership and zero mass for weighted divisors dominating the base now hold even if complete fibers lie in their union. The descended ideal model differs boundedly from the base ideal model, by cancellation, submersion pullback and direct model comparison; the proof needs no finite bound on the induced obstacle. The obstacle-envelope identity and all-obstacle equivalence retain their no-complete-fiber hypothesis.
subjects.boundary: The SGPT Kahler characterization retains its closed hypotheses. Density in the elementary ideal L1 metric does not characterize goodness. The new ordinary uniformity does not separate ordinary classes and is not a complete extension of the model topology. Canonical zero-obstacle envelope masses are finite in positive Hermitian backgrounds, although representatives may have infinite mass. The ordinary uniformity also depends on the fixed zero obstacle under smooth gauge changes, as proved on curves in Proposition 15.6.4. All-obstacle convergence restores smooth-gauge covariance but remains nonseparated on ordinary classes and incomplete on general curve models. Its analytic closure requires equality at every smooth obstacle. This is equivalent to zero-obstacle equality on curves and, in higher dimension, under bounded mass with positive lower volume of the ideal representative. Relative-envelope membership suffices in any smooth background; the remaining zero-lower-volume and no-BMP implications are unresolved here. Polar total variation remains the stronger complete curve-model topology. The fibration reduction permits any smooth real base form. Its all-obstacle conclusion uses relative-envelope membership unless the base is a positive curve. The unrestricted zero-obstacle implication remains unresolved, including backgrounds with unbounded mass.

active_formal_questions.label: qu:i-good-no-bmp
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{qu:i-good-no-bmp}
Extend the complete topology of \cref{thm:positive-model-complete-metric} to ordinary models of zero lower volume and beyond bounded mass, retaining analytic closure exactly at the ideal models. Recover the curve topology of \cref{cor:curve-model-completeness} and the background compatibility of \cref{sec:model-background-comparison,sec:two-sided-model-backgrounds}, including higher-dimensional limits that lose bigness or positive lower volume.

active_formal_questions.label: qu:nef-degeneration-exponent
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{qu:nef-degeneration-exponent}
Which geometric conditions on a nonclosed nef background force a common degeneration order, or an integral one? When is equality attained in the modification and residual order comparisons?

active_formal_questions.label: conj:lck-calabi-yau-vaisman
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{conj:lck-calabi-yau-vaisman}
A compact complex manifold with $c_1^{\mathrm{BC}}(X)=0$ that admits a strictly LCK metric admits a Vaisman metric.

active_formal_questions.label: conj:lck-lee-psef
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{conj:lck-lee-psef}
For every compact strictly LCK manifold, the ordinary Bott--Chern class $\{\kappa_\lambda\}$ is pseudoeffective.

active_formal_questions.label: q:lck-gauduchon-volume
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{q:lck-gauduchon-volume}
Does a compact LCK manifold have at most one Gauduchon LCK metric with a specified Lee class, specified twisted Bott--Chern class and specified smooth positive volume form?

active_formal_questions.label: qu:hermitian-i-characterization
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{qu:hermitian-i-characterization}
For a big nonclosed background on a manifold with bounded mass, find criteria for $\underline{\operatorname{vol}}_\theta(P_\theta[u]_{\mathcal I})>0$ in terms of restricted multiplier ideals or divisorial orders. When this lower volume vanishes, which implications between envelope equality and upper-volume equality in \cref{prop:conditional-i-characterization} remain valid?

active_formal_questions.label: qu:individual-equation-threshold
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{qu:individual-equation-threshold}\index{Subsolution!exact threshold equation problem}
Suppose $v_-(h)=0$. For a nonzero $0\leq f\in L^1(\mathrm{d}V)$ with $b_h(f)>0$, does there exist $u\in\PSH(X,h)$ such that
\[
 \mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_h(u)=b_h(f)f\,\mathrm{d}V?
\]
Determine the singularity or envelope class in which such an equation should be posed.

active_formal_questions.label: conj:nef-gaud-volume-big
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{conj:nef-gaud-volume-big}\index{Gauduchon variational volume!bigness conjecture}
Let $\theta$ be a nef smooth real $(1,1)$-background on a compact complex manifold. Then
\[
 \mathcal V_\mu(\theta)>0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \theta\text{ is big}.
\]
Here $\mu$ is any smooth strictly positive probability measure.

active_formal_questions.label: qu:gaud-metric-boundary
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{qu:gaud-metric-boundary}
For a specified finite-dimensional cone of smooth background classes, describe the metric completion of its unit-volume hypersurface. Which boundary points admit a current representative, and what estimates on the minimizing Gauduchon metrics distinguish finite from infinite distance?

active_formal_questions.label: conj:continuous-gaud-adjoint
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{conj:continuous-gaud-adjoint}\index{Adjoint measure!continuous-density conjecture}
For a Hermitian background $\omega$, the nonsingular reference $\varphi=0$, and every real $F\in C(X)$, the set $\mathcal A_0(F)$ consists of a single probability measure.

active_formal_questions.label: qu:singularity-topology-program
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{qu:singularity-topology-program}\index{Singularity type!topology problem}
Extend the complete metrizable topology of \cref{thm:positive-model-complete-metric} on ordinary models beyond bounded mass and positive lower volume, retaining analytic closure exactly at the ideal models. Preserve the smooth-gauge and two-sided background compatibility of \cref{sec:model-background-comparison,sec:two-sided-model-backgrounds}, and treat background limits losing bigness or a uniform positive lower-volume bound. Recover the complete polar-variation topology of \cref{cor:curve-model-completeness} on all curve models, and determine whether the higher-dimensional extension is completely metrizable.

active_formal_questions.label: qu:exact-trace-program
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{qu:exact-trace-program}
If $Y$ fails at least one of the two mass properties, can the Hermitian background $\Omega$ in \cref{thm:trace-profile-model-envelope} be chosen so that
\[
 \nu\bigl(\mathcal T_\Omega(u;Y)\circ\pi,E\bigr)
       =\tau_{Y,u}(E)
\]
for every prime divisor $E$ on every smooth modification $\pi$ of $Y$? If so, determine a background-compatible ordinary or ideal singularity class of this realization, and prove its addition and approximation properties.

active_formal_questions.label: qu:positive-system-recovery
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{qu:positive-system-recovery}
For a smooth big background on a manifold without bounded mass, find a condition on a compatible Hermitian envelope system that forces recovery of its ideal type at every finite parameter. It should recover the positive limiting lower-volume criterion of \cref{thm:positive-volume-system-recovery} when bounded mass holds. Specify the invariant and uniform estimates that replace the finite upper-volume deficit, and their behavior under modifications.

active_formal_questions.label: qu:partial-kernel-lower-program
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{qu:partial-kernel-lower-program}
Identify hypotheses on a weighted section series and its intrinsic growth dimension under which the partial Fubini--Study potentials attain the envelope lower bound and the normalized kernel measures converge. Relate the limiting measure to the Hermitian background while retaining the closed curvature and the growth dimension of the series.

active_formal_questions.label: qu:fiber-selected-approximation
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{qu:fiber-selected-approximation}
Let $\pi:X\to B$ be a surjective holomorphic submersion of connected compact complex manifolds with connected fibers, where $B$ is K\"ahler of dimension $q\geq1$. Fix a Hermitian form $\omega$ on $X$, a holomorphic line bundle $A$ with a smooth Hermitian metric $h$ on $B$, and $\varphi\in\PSH(X,\omega)$. Set $\theta=c_1(A,h)$. For positive integers $m$, identify
\[
 V_m=H^0\bigl(X,\pi^*A^m\otimes\mathcal I(m\varphi)\bigr)
          \subseteq H^0(B,A^m)
\]
by holomorphic descent. Find geometric or analytic conditions that produce $\psi\in\PSH(B,\theta)$ of positive non-pluripolar mass such that, for all sufficiently large $m$,
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 W_m=H^0\bigl(B,A^m\otimes\mathcal I(m\psi)\bigr)\subseteq V_m,\\
 \dim V_m-\dim W_m=o(m^q).
 \end{gathered}
\]
Determine which features of the singularities of $\varphi$ along the fibers suffice for this approximation.

active_formal_questions.label: prob:growing-jets-localization
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{prob:growing-jets-localization}
Let $C$ be a connected compact Riemann surface, let $x\in C$, and let $(L,h)$ be a smooth Hermitian holomorphic line bundle whose curvature is semipositive and strictly positive on $C\setminus\{x\}$. Fix an integer $r\geq1$. Suppose that in a local coordinate $z$ centered at $x$ and a holomorphic frame $e$ one has
\[
 |e|_h^2=\mathrm{e}^{-\phi},\qquad
 \phi(z)=|z|^{2r}+O(|z|^{2r+1}).
\]
Let $\nu$ be a smooth positive volume form with local expression $a(z)\,\mathrm{d}A$ and $a(0)=1$, where $\mathrm{d}A$ is Euclidean area. For positive integers $m$, choose integers $q_m\to\infty$ with $q_m=o(m)$. Give
\[
 V_m=H^0(C,L^m\otimes\mathfrak m_x^{q_m})
\]
the norm $\|s\|^2=\int_C|s|_{h^m}^2\,\mathrm{d}\nu$, where $\mathfrak m_x$ is the ideal sheaf of $x$. Write $B_m=\sum_j|s_{m,j}|_{h^m}^2$ for an orthonormal basis $(s_{m,j})$ of $V_m$, with value zero when $V_m=0$. Determine the growth ranges of $q_m$ for which, for each fixed real $\tau$, every sequence of points $x_m$ in the coordinate neighborhood satisfying
\[
 m|z(x_m)|^{2r}=q_m/r+\tau\sqrt{q_m/r}
\]
obeys
\[
 \frac{\pi B_m(x_m)}{mr^2|z(x_m)|^{2r-2}}
 \longrightarrow
 \Phi(\tau):=\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{-\infty}^{\tau}
                         \mathrm{e}^{-s^2/2}\,\mathrm{d}s.
\]
When this transition law fails, determine how further terms of the local weight change its center and scale.

active_formal_questions.label: qu:singular-space-equations-program
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{qu:singular-space-equations-program}
Beyond the projective-cone constructions of \cref{sec:projective-cone-equations}, determine geometric and measure conditions on compact unibranch Hermitian spaces that give existence and uniqueness in specified singularity classes. Identify estimates ensuring finite mass, descent and continuity, and their behavior under common refinements.

active_formal_questions.label: prob:primitive-elliptic-lower-mass
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{prob:primitive-elliptic-lower-mass}
Determine the lower Monge--Amp\`ere mass of the primitive elliptic bundles
above, in particular those of \cref{ex:primitive-elliptic-k3}.
Does it vanish whenever the real Chern class is nonzero?

active_formal_questions.label: qu:closed-nef-gaud-bridge
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{qu:closed-nef-gaud-bridge}
Let $\alpha$ be closed and nef with $\int_X\alpha^n>0$. Prove a positive lower bound for $\lambda_\mu(\alpha)$, and rule out the collapse in \cref{prop:gaud-positive-volume-collapse} for a sequence minimizing the bigness threshold of $\alpha$.

active_formal_questions.label: qu:geometric-gaud-endpoint
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{qu:geometric-gaud-endpoint}
Find geometric conditions beyond the metric identities in \cref{cor:geometric-determinant-bound} that imply the endpoint estimate in \eqref{eq:pvp-endpoint-geometric}, and identify how they exclude the lower-mass degeneration of \cref{sec:vanishing-lower-mass}.

active_formal_questions.label: qu:chern-ricci-gaud-singularities
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{qu:chern-ricci-gaud-singularities}
Suppose a Chern--Ricci flow has finite maximal time $\tau$ and $\mathcal V_\mu(\theta_\tau)>0$. Can one prove that $\theta_\tau$ is big and that the flow converges smoothly to a positive metric locally on $X\setminus E_{\mathrm{nH}}(\theta_\tau)$, without a bounded mass hypothesis? How do the annihilating Gauduchon currents describe the resulting degeneracy?

active_formal_questions.label: qu:balanced-pluriclosed-program
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{qu:balanced-pluriclosed-program}
Use the coexistence of a balanced metric and a pluriclosed metric to construct closed positive data, or to control a geometric flow that can change the torsion. Determine what estimate beyond the finite balanced trace prevents metric degeneration. Can determinant estimates for Gauduchon currents contribute to that estimate?

active_formal_questions.label: qu:hermitian-morse-program
active_formal_questions.text:
\label{qu:hermitian-morse-program}
Find geometric hypotheses controlling the cost in \eqref{eq:gaud-volume-subtraction-cost} up to a nef endpoint beyond the closed-core regime of \cref{thm:closed-core-subtraction}. Determine when positive root volume forces bigness without that core. For closed backgrounds, compare the estimate with classical Morse inequalities; for nonclosed backgrounds, retain the differential data and the dependence on $\mu$.
